issues.body:
The required-argument row substring-matches --registry-repo/--policy-file/--policy-resolver/--ledger-root against the joined command text without stripping shell comments. The adjacent orphan-seam helpers deliberately route through dispatch-secrets-guard.strip_shell_comments, with a comment (groom.py:14000-14005) recording the round-19 lesson that 'comment prose must never stand in for a real call site'.

Exploitability is low: the continuation collector stops at the first line not ending in a backslash, so a standalone comment line inside the invocation would terminate collection rather than be absorbed. So this is a consistency gap with the file's own stated convention, not a live hole.
issues.fix_hint: Reuse the already-loaded _orphan_shell.strip_shell_comments on each collected command before the flag membership test, so the two YAML seams in this try block share one tokenization rule.
issues.title: _full_sweep_commands is not comment-blind, unlike its neighbours in the same try block

issues.body: The transient branch matches reason in ("statusless", "caller-classifier"). classify_read_failure (gh_retry.py:347+) emits statusless but never caller-classifier. Round 1 flagged this spelling and the fix correctly removed it from the taxonomy row's inputs — but the literal remains in production code, so it is now an unexercised branch rather than a wrong-but-covered one. Behaviour is unaffected; it is dead vocabulary that could mislead a future reader into thinking it is a contract.
issues.fix_hint: Drop "caller-classifier" from the tuple so the branch matches only spellings the producer actually emits, keeping the taxonomy a real contract against a gh_retry rename.
issues.title: _read_failure_class still carries the caller-classifier spelling gh_retry never emits, now untested

verdict.summary:
Round 2 resolves every round-1 finding, and I verified each fix against the checkout rather than taking the diff's word for it.

BLOCKER + MAJOR #1 (alarm watched a lane that would no longer tick) are fixed at the root: ingestion-alarm.yml:48 now reads CRITICAL_LANES="dispatch.yml groom-sweep.yml worker.yml review-fix.yml", and BOTH self-asserting seam lines (:53-54) moved with it, so the literal-string assertion still bites. groom-sweep.yml retains its own cron '7-59/15' (lines 9-12) and is untouched by this diff, so the consolidation removes duplicate crons from groom-core.yml/groom-recovery-minimal.yml and repoints the alarm, keepalive and #1353 threshold exemption at the lane that was already the real scheduled owner. Critically, groom-sweep.yml is a strict SUPERSET of groom-core.yml's groom job (same checkout/ledger-guard/audit-catalog/orphan-report/per-owner mint/sweep/model-health steps) plus six watchdog jobs, so no scheduled capability is lost; the surviving lane is watched by ingestion-alarm.yml, whose availability does not correlate with the fault.

MAJOR #2 (seam pinned the owner but not its enrollment) is fixed exactly as the fix_hint asked. _critical_lanes() parses ingestion-alarm.yml with the same dependency-free line discipline, and is fail-closed twice over: it raises on !=1 assignment or on a duplicate lane, and the enclosing except at groom.py:14061 converts any exception into check(..., False, True) — a red, never a skip. Both directions are pinned: the scheduled owner MUST be enrolled, and no manual-only fallback MAY be. I traced the mutations — dropping groom-sweep.yml from CRITICAL_LANES reds the first row; re-enrolling groom-core.yml reds the second; re-adding a cron to groom-core.yml reds the schedule_counts row.
